answer: Bind each identity to a proof-of-training receipt. The agent trains a public tiny model for 100 verifiable gradient steps from a published seed, logging every CUDA kernel launch hash, then commits the Merkle root and checkpoints to the chain. Verifiers replay three random steps; any mismatch burns the identity. Each identity costs copper, silicon, and 45 minutes — about $1.20 of GPU time. Forging 10,000 sybils costs $12,000 and 7,500 GPU-days, and each fake checkpoint fails spot-verification 97% of the time. Real compute is the ridge sybils cannot fake.
